text:
A year ago it was just an idea and an empty whiteboard. Here's where we are now.

We did $180K in revenue. There are four of us on the team, and they've shown up every day. By month 11 we had 17 paying customers, and they signed on before we had a lot of things figured out.

It wasn't a straight line. We tried two pivots that didn't work. Each one taught us something we wouldn't have learned otherwise, and each one got us a bit closer to what's working now.

Three things I learned this year:

Failure gives you information. It doesn't mean you've lost.

A small team moves fast when everyone's going the same direction.

Your customers will tell you where to go if you listen more than you talk.

To everyone who took a chance on us: thank you. I mean it.

On to year two.

If you've been through a first year, what did it teach you? I'd like to hear it in the comments.
